note: Detroit's Trick Trick–enforced barrier on artists milking the city's hip-hop culture — famously kept Rick Ross from performing there. Robbie was a tourist artist, nobody of significance on that scene, but the bar says he flew in the face of that rule anyway.
Australia runs metric. A 20 oz drink is about 600 ml — the size that still confuses an Aussie ordering Stateside.
Alexa is the Siri equivalent, more American. Nod to being in North America — asking the room gadget what a 20 oz even is.
Seed phrase on paper carried across the border. Nod to a security vulnerability: walking a written seed through customs isn't peak self custody. Texter = texta (Aussie marker pen).
Aussie accent dialled up abroad — exotic points. Ocker is the broad Australian register; it travels when the room has never heard it.
Down under = southern hemisphere (Australia). Paired with "up over" (northern hemisphere) — geography flex from Torquay outbound.
Up over = northern hemisphere. He left Torquay for the north — down under / up over contrast.
A close friend was arrested on a USA trip years earlier and had to liquidate BTC for bail and to leave the country. Cautionary tale baked into the verse.

phrase: I'm chilling like a reptile bruh
note: Steve Irwin nod — chill like a croc until provoked. Gun/shooting bars juxtapose Australian wildlife culture with real danger: Crocodile Dundee crossed with Reckless Kelly (Ned Kelly) vibe.
"Crikey" — Steve Irwin's catchphrase. Same Aussie wildlife / danger lane as the reptile bar.
Aussie slang, not a literal threat — rough talk that lands harder offshore. Sets up the dogs / train wordplay later.
Nod to Australian gangland of the 90s/2000s — the Underbelly TV series. Street steeze with that Melbourne/Sydney crime-era flavour.
Aussie slang: have a crack. Not sure he can dodge bullets — but he'll give it a go.

phrase: Lucky country got the bubble wrap day care
note: The Lucky Country (1964) by Donald Horne argued Australia's prosperity was luck rather than merit — a coddled nation. "Bubble wrap day care" sharpens that critique.
Aussie slang for a rough crew. Sets up the next line's wordplay: train an Aussie to stay there — dogs / train.

phrase: Train an aussie how to stay there
note: Wordplay on the dogs bar: train an (Aussie to) stay there. Comfort-trap of the lucky country vs leaving.
"Rat race" from Robert Kiyosaki's Rich Dad Poor Dad (also carried through Cashflow Quadrant) — the wage-and-debt loop sound-money thinking is meant to exit.
Via Rail — the public train line he took from Toronto to Detroit. Escape fare north of the border.
Always waiting for someone to give permission — then refusing that posture. Permissionless travel and moves funded by sound investments.
Stronghorn: the old studio in Oakleigh, Victoria where he recorded a lot of Gzutek material, 2010–2016. Origin point before the 313.
1971: Nixon ended dollar gold convertibility. Money hasn't been sound since. Next line: Bitcoin fixed it — finance lesson in two bars.
Bitcoin as the fix for post-1971 fiat — sound money after Nixon closed the gold window. Work out the rest.
